The test image shows a soybean plant with a prominently darkened/necrotic stem (dark reddish-brown to black discoloration along the stem and petiole junction), with otherwise mostly green leaves showing minor small spots. The external stem discoloration is the key feature.

Top candidates: Phytophthora (dark brown stem lesions), Diaporthe (stem canker), Brown_Stem_Rot, Rhizoctonia.

Let me view the Phytophthora reference:

The Phytophthora reference bottom-right panel is a near-perfect match to the test image — it shows the same dark reddish-brown stem lesion at the node/petiole junction, with hairy stem texture and green leaves. This characteristic dark brown external stem discoloration spreading along the stem and at nodes is the hallmark of Phytophthora root and stem rot.
